default.notes: A visa from an Egyptian embassy or consulate is required before travel; the eVisa portal is not open to this nationality unconditionally.

groups.notes: Apply for the eVisa at visa2egypt.gov.eg (25 USD single entry) or buy the same 30-day visa on arrival for 25 USD cash at the airport bank counters before immigration.

eVisa and visa-on-arrival eligibility carries conditions for this nationality (a valid US, UK or Schengen visa or Gulf residence is commonly cited) — check visa2egypt.gov.eg; if the portal rejects the application, apply at an Egyptian consulate.
Citizens of Gulf Cooperation Council states can enter Egypt without a visa; stays of up to about 3 months are routinely granted.
A visa with additional security clearance is required — apply well in advance at an Egyptian embassy or consulate; processing can take several weeks.

EG.notes: Home country — no entry requirements for Egyptian citizens.

HK.notes: Hong Kong SAR passport holders can enter Egypt visa-free for up to 3 months.

MO.notes: Macao SAR passport holders can enter Egypt visa-free for up to 30 days.

MY.notes: Malaysian citizens can enter Egypt visa-free for short visits of up to 14 days; for longer stays apply for a visa in advance.

JO.notes: Jordanian citizens can generally obtain a 30-day visa on arrival; conditions can apply to some traveller categories — confirm before flying.

LB.notes: Lebanese citizens can obtain a visa on arrival subject to conditions (confirmed hotel booking or organised tourism is commonly required); otherwise apply at an Egyptian consulate.

SD.notes: Sudanese men aged roughly 18–49 need a visa before travel, while women, children and older travellers have been admitted without one — rules shift with the security situation, so confirm with an Egyptian consulate.

IL.notes: A visa is required for Egypt generally; Israeli citizens can, however, enter the Sinai resort strip (Taba to Sharm el-Sheikh) without a visa for up to 14 days via the Taba land crossing.
